abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) can act as a valuable partner for teachers. A particularly promising application is the use of AI as a hybrid-intelligence partner, leveraging eye-tracking data, to support students’ reading comprehension. This study examines the perceived preparedness and willingness of primary and secondary school teachers to adopt such technologies. Twenty teachers participated in semi-structured interviews. Vignettes were used to elicit reflections on system setups with different levels of human–AI collaboration. Participants expressed interest in technology that augments rather than replaces their professional role. Perceived benefits included visualising reading processes, supporting differentiation, enabling more independent student work, and providing feedback to adjust instruction. Ease of use was linked to intuitive dashboards and feasible classroom integration. Teachers emphasised the need for technological, pedagogical, subject-specific, and ethical knowledge, and identified trust and transparency as crucial. They also voiced concerns about reduced social interaction, screen-based reading, and possible erosion of human involvement. The exploratory findings point to the importance of hybrid-intelligence system designs that respect teachers’ autonomy and foreground usability, transparency, and pedagogical relevance. More broadly, the study offers insights for the design of hybrid-intelligent tools that respond to teachers’ needs and for a meaningful integration of technology into learning environments.

ur.ai_reason: 教师对AI系统视角的半结构化访谈研究
ur.tldr: 通过20位中小学教师参与的半结构化访谈与情境设计，探讨其对眼动数据驱动AI系统辅助学生阅读的看法与采纳意愿。教师期望技术增强而非替代自身专业角色，认为益处包括可视化阅读过程、支持差异化教学、促进学生独立学习、提供教学调整反馈；易用性取决于直观仪表盘与课堂整合可行性。教师强调需具备技术、伦理与教学知识，将信任与透明度视为关键前提，并担忧社交互动减少、屏幕化阅读及人文性削弱。

title: Hybrid intelligence in the classroom: teachers’ perspectives on eye-tracking data-driven AI systems to support students during reading tasks
title_zh: 课堂中的混合智能：教师对眼动数据驱动AI系统在阅读任务中辅助学生的看法
